UPDATE: Tesla is rolling out FSD (Supervised) v14.3.3 with the 2026.14.6.6 software update.

The release includes upgraded reinforcement learning a new vision encoder for low-visibility driving and a rewritten AI compiler that reportedly improves reaction times by 20%.

Tesla also increased Actually Smart Summon max speed from 6 mph to 8 mph.

The update improves lane decisions parking behavior traffic light handling at complex intersections and responses to emergency vehicles or rare road objects.

Tesla now also shows how many miles FSD has driven without intervention along with users’ longest intervention-free streaks directly on screen.

What’s new in FSD (Supervised) v14.3.3 (bundled as 2026.14.6.6 / 2026 Spring Update):
•  Actually Smart Summon max speed increased to 8 mph (13 km/h) — was 6 mph before.
•  New FSD distance tracker: Now shows total distance traveled without any interventions. The Self-Driving app also displays your longest intervention-free streak.
•  Improved handling of temporary system degradations.
•  Full merge with the 2026 Spring Update cabin features (Hey Grok voice assistant, rear display improvements, etc.).
